questions.prompt: Folded to the button at 100bb. Which hand is now an open that was a fold under the gun?
questions.explanation: The button acts last postflop and can open suited connectors that are folds from early position.

questions.prompt: The table is 6-handed instead of 9-handed. How should the earliest open change?

choices.text: Open wider. That seat plays more like a full-ring hijack than a 9-handed UTG.
Limp every hand because fewer players means less value.

questions.explanation: Short-handed, the first seat is later in a full-ring sense, so the open widens.

questions.prompt: Heads-up, you are the button and post the small blind. Which is true?

choices.text: You should fold every hand except premiums.
You act last preflop and first postflop.
You act first preflop and last postflop, and you open much wider than in a full ring.

questions.explanation: Heads-up the button acts first preflop, last after the flop, and opens a very wide range.

questions.prompt: Cutoff versus button at equal 100bb stacks, both folded to you. Who opens wider?

choices.text: Cutoff, because the button is forced to fold.
Button, because only the blinds remain and you act last postflop.

questions.explanation: The button steals wider. The cutoff still has the button left to act.
